note.what_happened: Marketing-qualified leads spiked to 93 on May 2, 2018, nearly double the expected level of 55 and substantially higher than the surrounding days (which ranged from 19 to 53). This represents a +5.1 standard deviation deviation from the predicted trend and seasonality pattern.
hypotheses: A marketing campaign or paid promotion launched on or just before May 2, driving an influx of qualified leads
A media mention, press coverage, or viral social media event occurred on May 1–2 that generated organic interest
Lead qualification criteria were temporarily loosened or a batch processing error inflated qualified lead counts on this specific day

note.what_happened: Marketing-qualified leads on Monday, January 22 reached 75, more than 70% above the expected level of 44 based on trend and weekly seasonality. This represents a +4.2 standard deviation spike, with surrounding days all substantially lower in the 18–42 range.
hypotheses: A campaign or promotional activity launched over the weekend (January 21–22) that drove inbound lead volume for the start of the business week.
A data collection or attribution change occurred on that specific date, causing leads from prior days to be backfilled or recategorized into January 22.
An unusually high-performing marketing channel or partner delivered a batch of qualified leads on this date due to a one-time event or offer.

note.what_happened: Marketing-qualified leads jumped to 71 on February 6th, nearly 70% above the expected 41.5 based on trend and weekly patterns. This represents a 4.0 standard deviation spike, with elevated values also seen on the surrounding days.
hypotheses: A promotional campaign or paid marketing initiative was launched on or just before February 5-6, driving increased lead volume through mid-week
A product launch, feature release, or major content piece went live and generated organic demand for qualified leads during this period
A lead quality or scoring model change was applied that reclassified or backfilled leads around this date, artificially inflating the counts

note.what_happened: Marketing-qualified leads dropped to 25 on May 1st, compared to an expected 54.5 based on trend and weekly seasonality—a shortfall of 29.5 leads. This represents a 4.0 standard deviation drop, the most severe deviation in the surrounding week.
note.calendar_context: Labour Day in Brazil (and many other countries), a major public holiday.
hypotheses: Reduced lead generation activity due to the public holiday reducing both company operations and customer inquiry volume.
A data collection or reporting system issue affecting May 1st records specifically.
Delayed or shifted lead intake where inquiries from May 1st were logged on May 2nd, which shows an anomalous spike to 93 leads.

note.what_happened: Marketing-qualified leads dropped to 10 on March 31, 2018, well below the expected 38 based on trend and seasonal patterns. This represents a 74% shortfall from forecast.
hypotheses: A marketing campaign was paused or ended on March 31 (end-of-quarter activity halt)
Lead qualification rules or processes were temporarily altered or turned off for weekend operations
A critical system or tool used to generate or qualify leads was unavailable on this specific date

note.what_happened: Marketing-qualified leads dropped to 19 on February 13, well below the expected 46.5. The surrounding days show typical lead volumes of 16–52, with leads recovering to 44 the next day.
hypotheses: A temporary disruption to lead generation or capture systems on this specific day
A scheduled pause in marketing campaigns or paid lead sourcing on February 13
Data collection or reporting error specific to this date

note.what_happened: Orders placed on 2017-11-24 reached 1176, more than five times the expected 227.5 based on trend and weekly seasonality. The following day (2017-11-25) showed a sharp drop to 499 orders, followed by a return toward normal levels.
note.calendar_context: Black Friday (United States shopping event, widely observed in Brazil's e-commerce sector).
hypotheses: Black Friday promotional event driving surge in order volume on this date.
System or data collection error resulting in inflated order counts for this day.
Promotional campaign or flash sale running specifically on 2017-11-24 that was not part of standard weekly patterns.

note.what_happened: Orders placed on 2017-11-25 reached 499, more than 2.5 times the expected level of 197.5. The preceding day (2017-11-24) had recorded an exceptional 1176 orders, with orders remaining elevated through 2017-11-27.
note.calendar_context: Black Friday (2017-11-24, US shopping holiday observed widely in Brazil and globally in e-commerce). The anomalous day falls on the Saturday immediately after Black Friday.
hypotheses: Continuation of Black Friday promotional activity and discounts extending into the following weekend day.
Delayed order processing or logging from the Black Friday peak spilling into 2017-11-25.
Cyber Monday preparation period (Cyber Monday 2017 was 2017-11-27) with extended promotion window across multiple days.

note.what_happened: Orders placed on Sunday 2017-11-26 reached 389, exceeding the trend and weekly seasonality forecast by 175 orders (+82%). This represents an 8.4 standard deviation spike, though notably lower than the preceding day (1,176 orders on Friday 2017-11-24).
note.calendar_context: Black Friday (2017-11-24 in Brazil) and the post-Black Friday period.
hypotheses: Black Friday extended promotional window: Brazilian retailers frequently extend Black Friday sales through the weekend, sustaining elevated order volume into Sunday

Delayed processing of Friday orders: A portion of the 1,176 orders placed on Friday 2017-11-24 may have been recorded or fulfilled on Sunday due to system capacity constraints or weekend processing delays
Cyber Monday preparation week: Some customers may have staggered purchases through the weekend ahead of Cyber Monday, creating a secondary demand wave

note.what_happened: Orders placed per day reached 403 on Monday 2017-11-27, which was 160 orders above the trend-and-seasonality forecast of 243.0. This represents a spike of 7.7 robust standard deviations above expected levels.
hypotheses: Orders placed on 2017-11-24 (Black Friday) were exceptionally high (1,176), suggesting a shopping event that may have driven delayed checkout activity or order fulfillment on the following Monday as customers processed purchases or returns.

The spike on Monday 2017-11-27 reflects a volume normalization after the Friday surge, with customers returning to place orders deferred from the weekend or affected by system capacity constraints during Black Friday.
A technical issue, operational change, or data recording anomaly on 2017-11-27 may have inflated the order count relative to surrounding days.

note.what_happened: Orders placed on May 16, 2018 reached 356, significantly exceeding the model's expected 219 based on trend and weekly patterns. This represents a +137 order increase (6.6 standard deviations above forecast).
hypotheses: A flash sale, limited-time promotion, or marketing campaign launched on May 16 that drove incremental order volume
A supply or inventory announcement (restock of popular items) that created urgency among customers
A payment method promotion or discount code activation on this specific date that was not active on surrounding days

note.what_happened: Orders placed on January 1, 2018 were 74, representing a drop of 136 orders (65%) below the model's expectation of 210 based on trend and weekly seasonality. This was the lowest observed level across the five-day window from December 29 to January 4.
hypotheses: The marketplace or its key logistics partners were closed or operating with minimal capacity on the national holiday, reducing customer ability to place orders.
Customers postponed purchases until after the holiday period, consistent with the strong recovery on January 2-4 when orders returned to or exceeded expected levels.
A combination of reduced platform staffing and customer behavior shifts typical of New Year's Day in Brazil suppressed order volume.
